draft.title: Inequality and sustainability
card: Environmental change does not affect all places equally. Poorer countries and communities often face the worst effects, even though they have usually caused the least of it.
Why they are exposed
Many poorer places are in areas prone to hazards such as floods, cyclones or drought. Their people may depend on farming or fishing, which weather and climate directly affect.
Why they struggle to cope
Poorer places often have less money for sea walls, early warning systems, insurance and rebuilding. This can make it harder to recover after a disaster.
Who caused it
Wealthier countries have generally released far more greenhouse gases per person, over a longer time. This is why many people argue that fairness matters in how the world responds.
draft.remember: Those who contributed least to environmental change can be hit hardest by it.

a.q: Which statement best describes the link between inequality and environmental change?
opts: Poorer places often suffer most while causing least
Poorer places cause most and suffer least
All places are affected to the same degree
Wealthier places suffer most and cause least
a.why: Poorer places are often more exposed and have fewer resources to cope, yet have usually released fewer greenhouse gases. The option saying all places are affected equally is wrong because exposure and ability to cope differ.
a.clue: Think about who causes the change and who copes with it.

b.q: Two coastal towns face the same sea level rise. Town X is in a low-income country with few resources. Town Y is in a wealthy country. Why is Town X likely to be harmed more?
opts: It has fewer resources to protect itself and recover
It has caused more greenhouse gas emissions than Town Y
Sea level rise only affects low-income countries
Its people have chosen not to prepare for hazards
b.why: Town X is likely to have less money for sea walls, warning systems and rebuilding, so the same hazard does more harm. The emissions option reverses the pattern, as poorer places have usually caused less.
b.clue: The hazard is the same, so look at the ability to cope.

a.best: Poorer places often suffer most while causing least

b.best: It has fewer resources to protect itself and recover

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier ("often"). The three distractors are all flat, absolute claims, so a student could pick the hedged option without knowing the idea. Add hedges to the distractors or remove "often".
